questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests hands-on ability to implement ephemeral, cost-controlled PR sandboxes using core Azure services and Azure DevOps, with proper secret management, feature flags, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- YAML pipelines and PR triggers
- Provisioning sandbox resources (Resource Groups, App Service, Azure SQL)
- Per-PR feature flags via Azure App Configuration
- Secrets management via Azure Key Vault
- Test automation and result publishing
- Automatic teardown on PR close or timeout with cost governance
- Observability via Azure Monitor Logs

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for PR sandbox pipeline
trigger: none

pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - main

variables:
  azureSubscription: 'Azure-Connection'
  location: 'eastus'
  resourceGroupName: 'pr-sandbox-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
  appServiceName: 'prapp-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
  sqlDatabaseName: 'prdb-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
  appConfigName: 'prconfig-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
  keyVaultName: 'prkeyvault-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
  costCap: '50'
  retentionHours: 48

stages:
  - stage: Provision
    displayName: 'Provision Resources'
    jobs:
      - job: CreateResources
        displayName: 'Create Sandbox Environment'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create Resource Group'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az group create --name $(resourceGroupName) --location $(location)
                az monitor log-analytics workspace create --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --workspace-name pr-sandbox-logs-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create App Service Plan and App Service'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az appservice plan create --name $(appServiceName)-plan --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --sku F1
                az webapp create --name $(appServiceName) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --plan $(appServiceName)-plan --runtime 'NODE|18-lts'

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create Azure SQL Database'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az sql server create --name prsqlserver$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --location $(location) --admin-user sqladmin --admin-password $(sqlAdminPassword)
                az sql db create --server prsqlserver$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --name $(sqlDatabaseName) --service-tier Basic

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create App Configuration'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az appconfig create --name $(appConfigName) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --location $(location)
                az appconfig kv set --name $(appConfigName) --key FeatureFlags.Enabled --value true --yes
                az appconfig kv set --name $(appConfigName) --key FeatureFlags.NewUI --value false --yes

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create Key Vault'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az keyvault create --name $(keyVaultName) --resource-group $(resourceGroupName) --location $(location)
                az keyvault secret set --vault-name $(keyVaultName) --name DatabaseConnectionString --value '$(connectionString)'

          - task: AzureKeyVault@2
            displayName: 'Retrieve Secrets'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              KeyVaultName: $(keyVaultName)
              SecretsFilter: '*'
              RunAsProxy: true

          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              ResourceGroup: $(resourceGroupName)
              # Add logging configuration

  - stage: Build
    displayName: 'Build and Test'
    dependsOn: Provision
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        displayName: 'Build and Run Tests'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            displayName: 'Install Node.js'
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'

          - script: |
              npm install
              npm run build
            displayName: 'Build Application'

          - script: npm run test:unit
            displayName: 'Run Unit Tests'

          - script: npm run test:integration
            displayName: 'Run Integration Tests'

          - task: PublishTestResults@2
            displayName: 'Publish Test Results'
            inputs:
              testResultsFormat: 'JUnit'
              testResultsFiles: '**/test-results.xml'
              failTestsOnFailure: false

  - stage: Teardown
    displayName: 'Teardown Resources'
    condition: or(eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'), eq(variables['System.PullRequest.PullRequestId'], ''))
    jobs:
      - job: DeleteResources
        displayName: 'Delete Sandbox Environment'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Delete Resource Group'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureSubscription)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az group delete --name $(resourceGroupName) --yes --no-wait
```

## Key Considerations

- **Cost Management**: Use F1 (free) tier for App Service, Basic tier for SQL, and set up budget alerts in Azure Cost Management.
- **Naming Convention**: Use PullRequestId in resource names to ensure uniqueness and easy identification.
- **Secrets Handling**: Use Azure Key Vault with Azure DevOps service connections for secure secret retrieval.
- **Timeout Policy**: Implement a scheduled pipeline run or use Azure Functions with timers to enforce the 48-hour cleanup.
- **Observability**: Integrate Azure Monitor for comprehensive logging and alerting.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests a practical disaster recovery drill workflow across regions, integrating infrastructure as code, secret management, governance, traffic control, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-region disaster recovery with Terraform and AKS
- Azure Key Vault per-environment secrets
- Policy-based governance and approvals
- Azure Front Door traffic shaping (canary) and health checks
- Drift detection via Log Analytics and automated rollback
- Auditability and rollback plan

## Code Example

```yaml
# DR drill pipeline sketch (high level)
stages:
- stage: DR
  jobs:
  - job: ProvisionDR
    steps:
    - task: TerraformCLI@0
      inputs:
        command: 'apply'
        workingDirectory: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/terraform/dr'
    - task: AzureKeyVault@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(serviceConnection)'
        KeyVaultName: '$(keyVaultName)'
        SecretsFilter: '*'
    - task: AzureFrontDoor@0
      inputs:
        action: 'update'
        routingRules: |
          - name: 'canary'
            percentage: 10
            backendPool: 'dr-region'
```

## Pipeline Steps

1. **Infrastructure Provisioning**: Deploy DR region resources using Terraform with remote state management
2. **Secret Management**: Retrieve environment-specific secrets from Azure Key Vault using managed identity
3. **Policy Gates**: Implement approval workflows and compliance checks before deployment
4. **Traffic Routing**: Configure Azure Front Door with 10%/90% canary traffic distribution
5. **Health Monitoring**: Deploy Log Analytics queries for drift detection and service health
6. **Automated Rollback**: Configure triggers for automatic failback based on health metrics
7. **Audit Logging**: Enable comprehensive logging across all pipeline stages

## Rollback Plan

- **Immediate Rollback**: Front Door traffic re-routing to primary region (100%)
- **Infrastructure Cleanup**: Terraform destroy DR resources if health checks fail
- **State Restoration**: Restore previous state from remote backend snapshots
- **Incident Documentation**: Generate audit report with root cause analysis

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This tests your ability to build ephemeral environments for PR reviews - a key DevOps skill. You need to show you understand AKS namespaces, Helm deployments, secret management, and cost control through automated cleanup.

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Azure DevOps Pipeline                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Trigger: PR created/updated                                 │
│  2. Create Namespace (pr-{PR_ID})                               │
│  3. Deploy Helm charts to namespace                             │
│  4. Inject Key Vault secrets                                    │
│  5. Run integration tests                                      │
│  6. Update PR with environment URL                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Complete Pipeline YAML

```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - '*'

variables:
  aksClusterName: 'ephemeral-aks-cluster'
  resourceGroup: 'rg-ephemeral-environments'
  helmVersion: '3.14.0'
  prNamespace: 'pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)'
  keyVaultName: 'kv-ephemeral-secrets'

stages:
  - stage: Setup
    displayName: 'Create PR Environment'
    jobs:
      - job: CreateNamespace
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Connect to AKS'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --name $(aksClusterName) --resource-group $(resourceGroup) --overwrite-existing

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create PR Namespace with Quotas'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                kubectl create namespace $(prNamespace) --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
                cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
                apiVersion: v1
                kind: ResourceQuota
                metadata:
                  name: pr-quota
                  namespace: $(prNamespace)
                spec:
                  hard:
                    requests.cpu: '4'
                    requests.memory: 8Gi
                    pods: '20'
                ---
                apiVersion: v1
                kind: LimitRange
                metadata:
                  name: pr-limits
                  namespace: $(prNamespace)
                spec:
                  limits:
                    - default:
                        cpu: '1'
                        memory: 2Gi
                      defaultRequest:
                        cpu: '100m'
                        memory: 256Mi
                      type: Container
                EOF

          - task: AzureKeyVault@2
            displayName: 'Fetch PR Secrets'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              KeyVaultName: $(keyVaultName)
              SecretsFilter: '*'
              RunAsPreJob: false

  - stage: Deploy
    displayName: 'Deploy to PR Environment'
    dependsOn: Setup
    jobs:
      - job: HelmDeploy
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Configure kubectl'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --name $(aksClusterName) --resource-group $(resourceGroup)

          - task: HelmInstaller@1
            displayName: 'Install Helm'
            inputs:
              helmVersionToInstall: $(helmVersion)

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Deploy Helm Release'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                helm upgrade --install pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber) ./charts/microservices 
                  --namespace $(prNamespace) --create-namespace 
                  --set image.tag=$(Build.BuildId) 
                  --set environment=pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber) 
                  --wait --timeout 5m

          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Create CSI SecretProviderClass'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
                apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1
                kind: SecretProviderClass
                metadata:
                  name: pr-azure-kv-secret
                  namespace: $(prNamespace)
                spec:
                  provider: azure
                  parameters:
                    useVMManagedIdentity: "true"
                    vaultName: "$(keyVaultName)"
                    secrets: |
                      - secretName: db-connection-string
                        objectName: "pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)-db-connection"
                        objectType: secret
                EOF

  - stage: Test
    displayName: 'Run Integration Tests'
    dependsOn: Deploy
    jobs:
      - job: IntegrationTests
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Run Isolated Tests'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                export DB_NAME="test_pr$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)_orders"
                export TEST_USER_PREFIX="pr$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)_test_"
                npm test -- --testPathPattern=integration

  - stage: Teardown
    displayName: 'Cleanup PR Environment'
    condition: eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest')
    jobs:
      - job: CleanupResources
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Delete Namespace & Helm Release'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --name $(aksClusterName) --resource-group $(resourceGroup) --overwrite-existing
                helm uninstall pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber) -n $(prNamespace) || true
                kubectl delete namespace $(prNamespace) --wait=true --timeout=5m || true
```

## TTL Cleanup Pipeline (Scheduled)

```yaml
trigger: none
schedules:
  - cron: '0 0 * * *'
    branches:
      include:
        - main

variables:
  aksClusterName: 'ephemeral-aks-cluster'
  resourceGroup: 'rg-ephemeral-environments'
  ttlHours: 48

pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'

steps:
  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Delete Expired PR Namespaces'
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az aks get-credentials --name $(aksClusterName) --resource-group $(resourceGroup) --overwrite-existing
        for NS in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.metadata.name=~"^pr-")]} {.metadata.name} {end}'); do
          AGE_HOURS=$(($(date +%s) - $(date -d $(kubectl get ns $NS -o jsonpath='{.metadata.creationTimestamp}') +%s)) / 3600)
          if [ $AGE_HOURS -gt $(ttlHours) ]; then
            helm uninstall -n $NS || true
            kubectl delete ns $NS --wait=true
          fi
        done
```

## Security Considerations

| Area | Implementation |
|------|----------------|
| Network Isolation | Azure Network Policy restricts pod-to-pod communication between PR namespaces |

5. **Resource Quotas**: Prevent PR monopolizing cluster resources

- Database naming: `orders_pr123`, `users_pr123`

- Use custom dimension `pr_id` in Application Insights to filter PR-specific telemetry

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to architect a multi-service, multi-region CI/CD flow in Azure DevOps, including selective builds, secure secret management, per-service approvals, and cross-region canary with rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Mono-repo service-level change detection
- Conditional jobs and environments per service
- Azure Key Vault integration for per-environment secrets
- Region-aware canary deployments via Azure Front Door
- Rollback strategy: redeploy last good artifact and pause production jobs

## Code Example

```yaml
# YAML skeleton (conceptual)
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
      - develop

variables:
  - group: 'global-config'
  - name: 'changedServices'
    value: ''

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  displayName: 'Detect Changed Services'
  jobs:
  - job: Detect
    displayName: 'Detect Changes'
    steps:
    - bash: |
        # Detect changed services using git diff
        changed=$(git diff --name-only $(Build.SourceVersion) $(Build.SourceBranch) | grep -E '^(services/[^/]+)/' | cut -d'/' -f2 | sort -u | tr '\n' ',')
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedServices;isOutput=true]${changed%,}"
      name: detectChanges

- stage: BuildAndTest
  displayName: 'Build and Test Services'
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: ne(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], '')
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - job: Build_${{ service }}
      displayName: 'Build ${{ service }}'
      steps:
      - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
        displayName: 'Build ${{ service }}'
        inputs:
          command: 'build'
          projects: 'services/${{ service }}/*.csproj'
      - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
        displayName: 'Test ${{ service }}'
        inputs:
          command: 'test'
          projects: 'services/${{ service }}/*.Tests.csproj'

- stage: DeployStaging
  displayName: 'Deploy to Staging'
  dependsOn: BuildAndTest
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - deployment: Deploy_${{ service }}_Staging
      displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }} to Staging'
      environment: '${{ service }}-staging'
      strategy:
        runOnce:
          deploy:
            steps:
            - task: AzureKeyVault@2
              displayName: 'Get Secrets from Key Vault'
              inputs:
                azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
                KeyVaultName: 'kv-${{ service }}-staging'
                SecretsFilter: '*'
            - task: AzureWebApp@1
              displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }}'
              inputs:
                azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
                appName: 'app-${{ service }}-staging'
                package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'

- stage: DeployProduction
  displayName: 'Deploy to Production'
  dependsOn: DeployStaging
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - deployment: Deploy_${{ service }}_Production
      displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }} to Production'
      environment: '${{ service }}-production'
      strategy:
        canary:
          increments: [10, 50, 100]
          preDeployGate:
            approval: '${{ service }}-prod-approval'
          deployGate:
            approval: '${{ service }}-prod-approval'
      steps:
      - task: AzureKeyVault@2
        displayName: 'Get Production Secrets'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          KeyVaultName: 'kv-${{ service }}-prod'
          SecretsFilter: '*'
      - task: AzureWebApp@1
        displayName: 'Deploy to Primary Region'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          appName: 'app-${{ service }}-prod-primary'
          package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'
      - task: AzureWebApp@1
        displayName: 'Deploy to Secondary Region'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          appName: 'app-${{ service }}-prod-secondary'
          package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'
      - task: AzureFrontDoor@1
        displayName: 'Update Front Door Routing'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          FrontDoorProfile: 'fd-${{ service }}'
          RoutingRule: '${{ service }}-routing'
          BackendPool: '${{ service }}-backend'
```

## Implementation Notes

- Use `git diff` to detect changed services at the directory level
- Implement conditional stages that only run when services have changed
- Leverage Azure DevOps environments for per-service approval gates
- Configure Azure Key Vault integration with service-specific vaults
- Implement canary deployments with incremental traffic routing
- Use Azure Front Door for region-aware traffic management
- Store rollback artifacts and implement automated rollback triggers

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design scalable cross-region release pipelines with policy gates and PR governance across many services.

## Key Concepts

- Multi-stage YAML pipelines
- Environments with approvals
- Azure Policy checks across subscriptions
- PR linking to Azure Boards
- Template-driven scalability

## Code Example

```javascript
# Minimal region template
parameters:
  - name: service
    type: string
  - name: region
    type: string

trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main

stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    steps:
      - script: echo "Build ${{ parameters.service }}"
        displayName: 'Build artifact'

- stage: Deploy
  dependsOn: Build
  environment: '${{ parameters.region }}'
  strategy:
    runOnce:
      deploy:
        steps:
          - script: echo "Deploy ${{ parameters.service }} to ${{ parameters.region }}"
```
